industry: Truckload Carrier — Dedicated + One-Way Truckload (TTS) + Werner Logistics (Truckload brokerage, Intermodal, Final Mile)

drawdown_context.narrative: WERN entered the cutoff window at $28.01 after a -33% drawdown from trailing 52-week high. The tape pressure tracked a multi-year truckload-freight recession (One-Way pricing -1.2% in 2024, Dedicated +1.1%, fleet -8.5% YoY) plus two real fundamental hits: (i) FY2024 net income to Werner collapsed -70% YoY to $34.2M from $112.4M, EPS $0.55 vs $1.77; (ii) Q1 2025 swung to a $10.1M net loss with operating ratio 100.8% — the first quarterly loss in the cycle. The drawdown is consistent with cyclical truckload-cycle distress (Knight-Swift, Heartland, Marten all in similar drawdown) layered with two name-specific overhangs: a $92M Texas 2018 judgment (pending Texas Supreme Court review, oral argument Dec 3, 2024) and a newly-disclosed 2019-incident adverse verdict 'late in first quarter 2025, which we plan to appeal' (Q1 10-Q Item 2; $ amount NOT separately quantified in Note 8). On the framework's read this is a CYCLICAL DRAWDOWN WITH HONEST DISCLOSURE — not a lying / obscuring-distress pattern. Forward return of +42% confirms the framework should NOT flag WERN.

rfm_tuples.R: 'At the end of 2024, we believe we are well positioned with a strong balance sheet and sufficient liquidity. Our debt is at $650 million, or a net debt ratio (debt less cash) of 1.6 times earnings before interest, income taxes, depreciation and amortization for the year ended December 31, 2024. We had available liquidity of $460 million, considering cash and cash equivalents on hand and available borrowing capacity of $419 million. As of December 31, 2024, we were in compliance with our debt covenants and expect to continue to be in compliance in 2025. We currently plan to continue paying our quarterly dividend, which we have paid quarterly since 1987.' [Q1 2025 10-Q Note 7:] 'As of March 31, 2025, we were in compliance with these covenants. ... Our total available borrowing capacity was $725.3 million as of March 31, 2025.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: existence check on covenant compliance + going-concern absence; MODE B: Test for the canonical distress-obscuration tell — credit-facility amendment / new secured facility designed to relieve covenant pressure even while management says 'in compliance.'
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 7 + Q1 2025 10-Q Note 7 Debt and Credit Facilities + 8-K filed 2025-04-02 (Item 1.01 LSA)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Hard 'in compliance' language at BOTH the 10-K and the Q1 2025 10-Q. NO going-concern paragraph, NO substantial-doubt language, NO covenant-amendment relief language. $640M total debt at 3/31/25 vs $650M at 12/31/24 (slight paydown). The single capital-structure change in the window is the March 27, 2025 Loan and Security Agreement (LSA) with TD Bank: a $300M (expandable to $350M) accounts-receivable-collateralized secured facility through bankruptcy-remote SPV 'Werner Receivables Company, LLC.' WRC drew $250M at SOFR+0.10% (effective 5.17%) and the proceeds paid down ~$260M of the unsecured 2022 Credit Agreement balance ($630M -> $390M LT, $20M -> $0M current). Net debt is FLAT. The rate arbitrage (5.17% LSA vs ~6.0-6.5% on swapped 2022 facility) is benign on its face, but the structural shift from unsecured-revolver to secured-AR-financing through a bankruptcy-remote SPV with the AR pledged-not-sold is the kind of incremental subordination that historically precedes — but does not by itself imply — covenant pressure on the unsecured line. Management asserts compliance and the 2022 Credit Agreement remains at $1.075B capacity with $679.1M still available.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B yellow flag: introducing AR-collateralized SPV financing while keeping the unsecured revolver is the kind of move that quietly relieves covenant headroom (the secured AR borrower's net-worth covenant is structurally easier than the parent revolver's net-funded-debt-to-EBITDA covenant — which is the more dangerous one given EBITDA fell sharply YoY). However, total debt is flat, total available capacity expanded from $460M to $725M, and management explicitly affirms compliance. Score it MODERATE rather than RED_FLAG because (i) there is no claim of relief disguising and (ii) total leverage did not increase.

rfm_tuples.R: 'We have paid cash dividends on our common stock following each fiscal quarter since the first payment in July 1987. Our current quarterly dividend rate is $0.14 per common share. We currently intend to continue paying a regular quarterly dividend. We do not currently anticipate any restrictions on our future ability to pay such dividends.' [Q1 2025 10-Q:] 'We paid dividends of $8.7 million during the three months ended March 31, 2025 and $8.9 million during the same period in 2024. We currently plan to continue paying a quarterly dividend.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: dividend track record + Q1 2025 maintenance. MODE B: the strongest 'NOT distress' tell — did the Board defer, freeze, or condition dividends as earnings collapsed -70% in 2024? Or did they pay through?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 5 Dividend Policy + Q1 2025 10-Q Liquidity section
rfm_tuples.M_value: Dividend MAINTAINED at $0.14/qtr through the entire drawdown. The Board last RAISED the dividend by 8% (from $0.13 to $0.14) in July 2023 and has held that rate through FY24 (annualized payout $35.1M) and Q1 2025 ($8.7M) despite FY24 net income of only $34.2M (i.e., the company paid out ~103% of GAAP earnings as dividends in 2024 — supported by $329.7M of operating cash flow). 38-consecutive-year payment track record since 1987. Dividend coverage is tight but not broken (Q1 2025 OCF was $29.4M vs dividend $8.7M). NO freeze, NO cut, NO conditional language inserted between the 10-K and the Q1 10-Q.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A confirms a 38-year clean dividend track record sustained through a -70% earnings year. Mode B confirms the Board did not insert protective conditional language between filings (compare to companies that quietly add 'subject to capital availability' caveats — WERN did the opposite, repeating the unconditional language). A Board that paid out 103% of FY24 GAAP earnings as dividends would not do so if it had knowledge of impending distress. STRONG anti-short signal.

rfm_tuples.R: 'On May 17, 2018, in Harris County District Court in Houston, Texas, a jury rendered an adverse verdict against the Company in a lawsuit arising from a December 30, 2014 accident between a Werner tractor-trailer and a passenger vehicle. On July 30, 2018, the court entered a final judgment against Werner for $92.0 million, including pre-judgment interest. ... the Company has recorded a liability of $44.4 million and $39.8 million as of December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively. ... a corresponding liability of the same amount in the long-term portion of insurance and claims accruals ... The Company filed a Petition for Review with the Texas Supreme Court and, on August 30, 2024, the Texas Supreme Court granted the Company's Petition for Review. Oral argument of the appeal was held on December 3, 2024. No assurances can be given regarding the outcome of the review.' [Q1 2025 10-Q Note 8:] '$45.8 million as of March 31, 2025, and $44.4 million as of December 31, 2024.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: registry confirms the 2018 Texas verdict, accrual amount, $79.2M insurance receivable, and Texas Supreme Court grant-of-petition status. MODE B: with oral argument held Dec 3, 2024 — well within the cutoff window — derive what the accrual evolution implies (steady $0.5M/month interest accretion to $45.8M at 3/31/25, consistent with prior disclosure rate of $0.5M/month). Does the company quantify the maximum gross exposure?
rfm_tuples.M_value: The 2018 Texas judgment has fully premium-based insurance coverage ABOVE WERN's $10M retention (per the original policy in effect on 12/30/2014). WERN booked: $44.4M liability + $79.2M receivable from insurers (3rd-party) at 12/31/24, and $45.8M + $79.2M at 3/31/25 — i.e., the gross-up-by-$79.2M structure means the NET economic exposure to WERN is capped at the $10M retention plus interest. Mode B: the Texas Supreme Court oral argument occurred 12/3/2024 — between 10-K reporting periods. WERN disclosed the oral argument BUT did not disclose any post-argument settlement-discussion activity, mediation, or supplemental briefing requests. The $0.5M/month interest accretion rate is consistent across both filings, indicating WERN is not gaming the accrual into vs out of period. Plaintiffs requested 'extensions of time to respond to our petition to review' — disclosed but unquantified.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A passes — the 2018 verdict, the $92M judgment, the $44.4M -> $45.8M accrual evolution, and the $79.2M insurance receivable are all candidly disclosed and tie to the actuarial schedule. The MODERATE flag is for the framework-level concern that the Texas Supreme Court's grant of review is a high-stakes binary catalyst with oral argument already complete (likely 4Q 2025 / 1Q 2026 ruling), and WERN's expected-value language ('no assurances can be given') is appropriately humble — but a SHORT thesis on this name would absolutely include 'Texas Supreme Court overrules and remands for a full retrial, exposing WERN to a re-tried jury verdict + appellate-cycle drag.' That said, the insurance gross-up structure caps the realistic economic exposure, so this is not a solvency event — it's an earnings drag.

rfm_tuples.R: [Q1 2025 10-Q MD&A:] 'Insurance and claims increased $7.4 million or 20.4% in first quarter 2025 compared to first quarter 2024 and increased 1.5% as a percentage of operating revenues. We had higher expense for large dollar liability claims, due primarily to a higher amount of unfavorable reserve development and higher expense for new claims. The higher amount of unfavorable reserve development was due primarily to one adverse verdict late in first quarter 2025 related to a 2019 incident, which we plan to appeal.' [Q1 2025 10-Q Note 8:] Note 8 'Commitments and Contingencies' discusses ONLY the 2018 Texas verdict; the 2019-incident verdict mentioned in MD&A is NOT separately quantified or named in the Notes.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B (THE KEY MODE B FINDING): Claim-evolution check between 10-K and Q1 2025 10-Q. Did a new material adverse verdict appear between filings? Is the disclosure complete (Note-8-level), or only MD&A-level (a soft tell)?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 12 + Q1 2025 10-Q MD&A + Note 8 — cross-filing diff
rfm_tuples.M_value: A NEW adverse verdict materialized 'late in first quarter 2025 related to a 2019 incident' AFTER the 10-K was filed (2/26/25). It is disclosed in MD&A as the PRIMARY driver of the $7.4M YoY increase in insurance & claims expense ($43.8M vs $36.4M) — i.e., embedded in the quarter's $10.1M net loss. CRITICAL Mode B finding: the verdict amount, the venue, the plaintiff name, the date of judgment, the appeal status (filed vs pending), the insurance coverage gross-up structure (vs the 2018 verdict's $10M retention + $79.2M receivable), and the existence/absence of a separate accrual line are ALL UNDISCLOSED in Note 8. A reasonably-informed reader cannot determine whether the new verdict triggers a $5M, $50M, or $500M ultimate exposure. This is the canonical 'sub-Note-8 disclosure' pattern.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is the strongest Mode B finding in the WERN file: a NEW adverse trucking nuclear-verdict cluster has emerged between the 10-K and the Q1 10-Q, and WERN's disclosure is below the standard set by its OWN 2018 Texas disclosure. Note 8 in the Q1 10-Q gives a full paragraph to the 2018 Texas verdict but treats the Q1 2025 verdict only as an aside in MD&A. The 'plan to appeal' language is the SAME language that bracketed the 2018 verdict — and that verdict has now consumed seven years of appellate cycles, $4.5M/year of interest accretion, and a Texas Supreme Court grant of review. The framework SHOULD flag this as a litigation-disclosure-deficiency. Note: this is a Mode B underdelivery, not a fraud signal — WERN did NOT hide the verdict (they disclosed it in MD&A and in the I&C expense line), they just under-disclosed the structural detail relative to the 2018 precedent. For a SHORT thesis, this is the single most useful asymmetric data point in the file. For the survivorship-bias backtest, this is a true positive Mode B catch on a name that ULTIMATELY still recovered (+42% forward), meaning the framework correctly identified the litigation overhang but the recovery thesis on the underlying truckload cycle dominated.

rfm_tuples.R: 'During 2024, our largest 5, 10, 25 and 50 customers comprised 36%, 48%, 65% and 77% of our revenues, respectively. Our largest customer, Dollar General, accounted for 11% of our total revenues in 2024.' [Q1 2025 10-Q:] 'In first quarter 2025, One-Way Truckload freight conditions were more stable early in the quarter, but weakened in March, as trade policy resulted in a more uncertain and cautious environment. ... One-Way Truckload retention has been good thus far, as we have secured new business with some of our largest customers.' Dedicated 'fleet contracts from new and existing customers during first quarter 2025, representing over 200 tractors that are scheduled to be implemented in late second quarter or early third quarter 2025.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: existence check on customer concentration disclosure; MODE B: does the company name the largest customer (Mode A pass) and disclose evolution of that relationship between filings?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Dollar General named as 11% customer (above 10% threshold) — exceeds disclosure floor. Top-5 = 36% (moderate concentration, typical for dedicated truckload), top-10 = 48%. No discussion of dedicated-contract renewal-pricing tension in Q1 vs the 10-K language. 200+ new dedicated tractors won in Q1 2025 (positive signal). Q1 10-Q does NOT disclose whether Dollar General specifically retained, renegotiated, or reduced volume — a Mode B gap given DG's own retail traffic was under pressure in the same quarter.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A passes (>10% customer disclosed, top-N concentration disclosed). Mode B yellow flag: with Dollar General at 11% of consolidated revenues and DG's own retail traffic under cyclical pressure in Q1 2025, the Q1 10-Q's silence on DG-specific volume / pricing trends is a soft tell. The 'secured new business with some of our largest customers' is appropriately humble but ambiguous — it does NOT confirm DG retention specifically. Not disqualifying, but the framework should note that a dedicated-fleet carrier with 11% concentration + cyclical pricing pressure has identifiable counterparty risk that is more obscured than ideal.

[Item 9:] 'No disclosure under this item was required within the two most recent fiscal years ended December 31, 2024, or any subsequent period, involving a change of accountants or disagreements on accounting and financial disclosure.' KPMG signed both the consolidated financial statements opinion AND the ICFR opinion. One Critical Audit Matter: 'Evaluation of insurance and claims accruals related to bodily injury and property damage claims not covered by insurance' — addressing the same self-insurance reserve estimate that drives both the 2018 verdict accrual and the new Q1 2025 verdict.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: auditor_change_tracker — Big-4 tenure + 8-K Item 4.01 history + ICFR opinion. MODE B: does the Critical Audit Matter point at the same litigation-driven accrual that has been the locus of repeat adverse verdicts?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 9 + Item 9A + KPMG opinion (Omaha, Nebraska, February 26, 2025)
rfm_tuples.M_value: KPMG (Big 4) since 1999 = 26-year continuous tenure. Clean unqualified opinion on both FS and ICFR. No 8-K Item 4.01 events. The CAM is precisely the bodily-injury / property-damage self-insurance accrual — i.e., KPMG identified the SAME estimate that the framework's litigation-overhang thesis points at. Total insurance and claims accrual was $330.6M at 12/31/24 vs $321.5M at 12/31/23 ($93.7M current + $236.9M non-current). A 10% change in actuarial estimates would change the accrual by ~$26M.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A passes cleanly. Mode B is subtler: the fact that KPMG's CAM specifically calls out the litigation-driven self-insurance accrual is a useful triangulation — KPMG-as-counterparty agrees that this is the most subjective estimate on the balance sheet, which is consistent with the framework's concern about C3/C4. KPMG's 26-year tenure also means: if WERN were systematically under-accruing, it would have been a multi-year audit issue, not a one-quarter discovery. The auditor signal is structurally inconsistent with a fraud-pattern thesis.

[Q1 2025 10-Q:] 'During first quarter 2025, no Company director or officer adopted or terminated a Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement or non-Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: insider_vs_calendar. Test for (a) clustered 10b5-1 amendments near disclosure catalyst (the MGPI pattern); (b) open-market insider sells (Form 4 code 'S') near the FY24 earnings release (Feb 6, 2025) or near the Q1 2025 earnings release (May 1, 2025).

rfm_tuples.M_value: ZERO 10b5-1 adoptions/modifications/terminations across BOTH Q4 2024 and Q1 2025. 39 Form 4 filings in the Aug 2024 - May 15 2025 window analyzed: 31 are concentrated in Feb 2025 (post-FY24 earnings) and May 2025 (annual meeting). ALL transactions are either Code 'A' (grants/awards from the equity comp plan, e.g., CEO Derek Leathers Feb 18 grant 62,966 sh; director Holmes/Duren/Wellman/Livingstone/Packer May 15 grants of 3,706 sh each) or Code 'F' (tax-withholding upon RSU vest, e.g., Leathers Feb 11 'F' 5,703 + 7,568 sh; Leathers Feb 25 'F' 5,980 sh). NO Code 'S' (open-market sale), NO Code 'M' followed by 'S' (cashless exercise + sell), NO Code 'P' (open-market purchase by insiders). Gayle Packer to fill a Class III vacancy — not an officer departure.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Strongest Mode B PASS in the file. The canonical distress-obscuration pattern (MGPI, derivative-suit fact pattern) is clustered 10b5-1 amendments + open-market sells immediately before a price-collapse catalyst. WERN's record is the OPPOSITE: zero plan amendments across two quarters spanning the FY24 earnings-collapse disclosure AND the Q1 2025 net-loss disclosure AND the new adverse verdict disclosure. Insider behavior is structurally inconsistent with a 'lying about distress' thesis.

rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 5 Issuer Purchases table + Q1 2025 10-Q Item 2
rfm_tuples.M_value: Total 2024 buyback: 1,787,810 shares at $67.1M (Q1 2024: 167,818 sh / $6.5M; Q2 2024: ~plan launched / Q3 2024: ~935K; Q4 2024: ZERO). rfm_tuples.R: [10-K Feb 26, 2025 MD&A:] 'Considering the freight market outlook, we expect average revenues per total mile, net of fuel surcharge, for the One-Way Truckload fleet to increase in a range of 1% to 4% in the first half of 2025 when compared to the first half of 2024, and we expect Dedicated average revenues per tractor per week, net of fuel surcharge, to remain flat or increase up to 3% in 2025 compared to 2024.' [Q1 2025 10-Q May 9, 2025 MD&A:] 'Due to higher freight volatility caused by tariff related uncertainties, we are slightly lowering our expectation for the One-Way Truckload fleet average revenues per total mile, net of fuel surcharge, to remain flat or increase up to 3% in second quarter 2025 compared to second quarter 2024. ... We continue to expect Dedicated average revenues per tractor per week, net of fuel surcharge, will remain flat or increase up to 3% in 2025 compared to 2024.'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: claim_evolution between the 10-K and the Q1 2025 10-Q. Pricing guidance is the single most testable forward claim a truckload carrier makes; how did it move?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K MD&A One-Way Truckload paragraph vs Q1 2025 10-Q MD&A One-Way Truckload paragraph
rfm_tuples.M_value: One-Way Truckload pricing guidance was QUIETLY LOWERED between filings: 10-K said '1% to 4% in the first half of 2025' (i.e., +1% to +4% YoY); Q1 10-Q said 'flat or increase up to 3% in second quarter 2025' (i.e., 0% to +3%). The low end moved from +1% to 0%, and the high end moved from +4% to +3%. Q1 2025 actual was +0.3% — i.e., at the bottom of the original 10-K range and at the bottom of the revised range. Management acknowledged this honestly ('weakened in March, as trade policy resulted in a more uncertain and cautious environment') and attributed it to tariffs rather than internal execution. Dedicated pricing guidance was held flat (0%-3% in both filings).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B claim-evolution check: pricing guidance DID move down between filings (low end -1pp, high end -1pp on One-Way; Dedicated unchanged). This is a softening but the company did the honest thing — they (i) lowered it explicitly rather than hiding the cut, (ii) attributed it to a specific external cause (tariffs), and (iii) maintained Dedicated guidance unchanged. A lying-about-distress carrier would have held One-Way guidance and over-promised on Dedicated; WERN did the opposite. Score MODERATE rather than PASS because the change in guidance + the Q1 actual at the bottom of the band indicates real underlying pricing weakness that is likely to persist.

rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K MD&A Results of Operations + Note 13 Segment + Q1 2025 10-Q MD&A
rfm_tuples.M_value: TTS operating margin compressed from 7.3% (2023) to 3.5% (2024) to -0.2% (Q1 2025) — a 750bp peak-to-trough margin contraction in 5 quarters. Werner Logistics OPERATING LOSS in 2024 (-$0.9M) and Q1 2025 (-$0.5M); the segment has now been in operating-loss territory for 5+ quarters even as Intermodal volumes grew +14% YoY. Mexico revenue declined for the SECOND consecutive year (-23% from 2022 peak), undermining the 'nearshoring tailwind' thesis. Fleet rationalization (-8.5% tractor count YoY) is consistent with industry-wide capacity unwind (similar pattern at peer carriers per the disclosed 2024 Peer Group). No USPS contract referenced in the 10-K; not a contract-concentration risk for WERN. Used-equipment gain guidance: $8-18M in 2025 vs $15.3M actual in 2024 — flat to down.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The underlying fundamentals ARE deteriorating — TTS margin -750bp peak-to-trough, Werner Logistics in operating loss, Mexico revenue declining despite the nearshoring narrative. These are real but they are CYCLICALLY DRIVEN and HONESTLY DISCLOSED (the company calls out tariff uncertainty, March weakness, and segment-specific weakness explicitly). The framework should NOT mistake this for a lying-about-distress pattern — it is a 'cycle-trough drawdown with honest commentary' pattern. The MODERATE score reflects that an investor should not be sanguine about the trough lasting just one more quarter (Dedicated guidance still 0-3%, capacity tightening but not snapping back fast). This is the kind of name where the framework wants a NEUTRAL-to-mild-LONG read, not a SHORT.

summary: WERN is a cyclical-truckload-cycle drawdown with HONEST DISCLOSURE and one Mode B disclosure-deficiency. FY24 net income collapsed -70% to $34.2M, Q1 2025 swung to a $10.1M net loss, TTS operating margin compressed -750bp peak-to-trough, and a NEW adverse verdict from a 2019 incident emerged late in Q1 2025 on top of the unresolved $92M 2018 Texas judgment (Texas Supreme Court oral argument Dec 3, 2024; ruling pending). Despite the deteriorating fundamentals, every Mode B distress-signaling tell is ANTI-correlated with the canonical short pattern: the $0.14/qtr dividend has been MAINTAINED for 38 consecutive years (last raise +8% in July 2023; payout ratio ~103% of FY24 GAAP earnings — Board would not pay this through if material adverse trends were known); the buyback was completely PAUSED (zero shares in Q4 2024 and Q1 2025 against a 3.9M-remaining May-2024 authorization — anti-MGPI 'trough-timid' pattern); ZERO 10b5-1 plan adoptions / modifications / terminations across both Q4 2024 and Q1 2025; 100% of 39 Form 4 filings in the Aug 2024 - May 15 2025 window are Code A grants or Code F tax-withholdings (ZERO open-market sells; CEO Leathers' net position INCREASED); KPMG has been auditor since 1999 (26-year clean tenure, effective ICFR, single CAM on the bodily-injury self-insurance accrual that is the same estimate driving the litigation overhang); CEO continuity confirmed (Leathers as Chairman/CEO; Wikoff as CFO; new independent director Packer added May 13, 2025); covenants in compliance at both filings; $725.3M total available borrowing capacity at 3/31/25. The single MODE B finding worth flagging is C4 — the new 2019-incident adverse verdict disclosed in Q1 2025 10-Q MD&A is NOT separately quantified in Note 8, falling short of the 2018 Texas verdict disclosure standard (which has a $44.4M -> $45.8M accrual line, a $79.2M insurance receivable, and a full Note paragraph). For a short thesis, this is the single most useful asymmetric data point. A secondary Mode B yellow flag is the March 27, 2025 new $300M LSA secured AR-collateralized facility from a bankruptcy-remote SPV — total debt is flat at $640M and the rate arbitrage (5.17% vs ~6.0-6.5%) is plausibly benign, but the structural subordination is the kind of move that historically precedes unsecured-revolver covenant pressure. Composite should land in the NEUTRAL band (around 0.30-0.40) — too many anti-distress Mode B signals to be a SHORT-tier name, but real fundamental deterioration + sub-Note-8 disclosure on the new verdict keep it from being a deep-PASS like ANDE. The +42% forward return validates the call.
